post.caption: Baroque probably began as a pearl word. A baroque pearl is noticeably irregular, with no apparent symmetry. Dictionaries say it likely comes from Portuguese barroco, an irregular pearl, and only later did the word name an art style. Around 1600 goldsmiths used lumpy pearls as the bodies of creatures. In a Met pendant, one pearl is a sea monster's body. Another pendant uses a pearl for the torso of a centaur. A Cheapside Hoard pin has a pearl for a ship's hull. Its mast and rigging are made of gold wire. The hoard was unearthed in London in 1912.
